text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Embattled black businessman Strive Masiyiwa's dream to launch a cellular phone network appeared to crumble this week when the government reaffirmed its earlier decision not to issue a third cellular phone licence and ordered him to immediately dispose of his multi-million-dollar equipment which he set up three years ago.
- A consortium of local black business leaders has acquired a 21 percent stake valued at more than Z$100 million in South African-based engineering and construction group IHL.

- The board of directors at Zimbabwe's trade promotion body, Zimtrade, this week engaged an external auditor to examine the group's accounts, weeks after sending chief executive Morrison Sifelani on forced leave.
- The Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe is said to be losing up to Z$1 million every month in potential net rentals by keeping empty its former 12-storey headquarters.

- Zimbabwe's first privately owned airline, Zimbabwe Express, this week said the strike at state-owned rival Air Zimbabwe was hurting its business, with 30 to 40 percent of its clients thinking all airlines in the country were not operating.
- A multi-million-dollar tile manufacturing company, the second of its kind in Zimbabwe, has been launched with the backing of three prominent black businessmen.
- The Zimbabwean government has said it will not issue a third cellular phone operating licence as had initially been planned.

- Thirty-five tour and safari operators in Zimbabwe will soon appear in court for illegal trophy hunting and overhunting involving more than Z$80 million in a scam alleged to involve some officials from the department of national parks and wild life management.
